newsitem.title: USA: Duke postpones Oconee 2 S.C. nuke restart.
newsitem.headline: Duke postpones Oconee 2 S.C. nuke restart.

text.p: Duke Power Co again delayed electricity production from its 846 megawatt (MW) Oconee nuclear power unit 2 while the company continues further restart testing, a company spokesman said.

The company originally said the unit would resume power output over the weekend, then pushed the restart back to the middle of this week, but the unit is not now expected to restart before Friday, said spokesman Rick Zuercher.
"It's not coming up today or tomorrow," Zuercher said Wednesday.
The unit, located in Seneca, S.C., was shut Sept 24 after a steam pipe burst in the non-nuclear side of the plant, scalding seven workers.
The spokesman said delays in synchronizing to the electricity grid were not uncommon when restarting a unit that has been down several months.
"When a unit has been down for a long time it's hard to project when you're going to come on line," he said.
"The main thing is not to get it back on line in a hurry but to get it back on line so it can stay on line for a long time."
Zuercher said Duke has arranged for adequate power supply to meet the company's needs during the Oconee outage.
The adjacent Oconee nuclear power units 1 and 3, each with a capacity of 846 megawatts, were shut Oct 4 for steam pipe inspections and both are expected to resume power output in February.
Duke Power has a total generating capacity of about 18,500 MW, of which the Oconee complex accounts for 14 percent.
